text: Lesson 13 tested the failover group on the DBA's own terms — planned, expected, full attention. This drill is different. Overlook's leadership, the same board that mandated this entire project, triggers an unannounced test, specifically to find out whether the DR runbook holds up under realistic pressure, not just under ideal conditions.

The drill starts the way a real incident would. The on-call DBA has to open the actual runbook document, check its trigger criteria, run the exact failover command exactly as documented, work through the verification checklist, and communicate status while the failover is still in progress.

This has the DBA working from a document instead of from memory, under real pressure, with leadership watching whether the process, not just the technology, actually holds up. The honest response is the same discipline a real incident demands: no improvising, no skipping steps, no under-reporting a problem just to make the drill look clean.
Next lesson checks the drill's actual, observed numbers against Lesson 11's RPO and RTO targets, honestly — whether they were actually met or not.
